# Bug Report — docker-gems

**Generated by:** read-only investigation agent
**Repository:** `c:\x\docker-gems`
**Scope:** shell scripts, Dockerfiles, CI/CD, Kubernetes manifests, Python scripts, version consistency

---

## Summary

The most impactful finding is a **widespread pattern of missing `apt-get upgrade -y`** in seven
production-stage Dockerfiles that do call `apt-get install`. AGENTS.md requires every image that
uses `apt-get install` to run `apt-get upgrade -y` first ("Install the security updates of the
base image before the tools"). The omission leaves known CVEs in the base image packages.
Separately, the GitLab CI smoke test for `java-eks` does not verify HTTP 200 — `wget` succeeds
on any redirect, so the test can pass while the application is broken. A comment in the
GitHub Actions workflow says to pin `trivy-action` to a full commit SHA, but the code uses a
mutable version tag.

## High

### H-1 · Seven production Dockerfiles are missing `apt-get upgrade -y`

| File | Base image |
|------|-----------|
| `rust-desktop/Dockerfile` | `rust:latest` (Debian) |
| `java-ui-browser/Dockerfile` | `eclipse-temurin:27-jdk-resolute` (Ubuntu) |
| `rust-node/Dockerfile` | `rust:latest` (Debian) |
| `codegraph/Dockerfile` (final stage) | `node:latest` (Debian) |
| `allure/Dockerfile` (final stage) | `node:slim` (Debian) |
| `code-quality/Dockerfile` (final stage) | `debian:stable-slim` |
| `web-qa/Dockerfile` | `python:latest` (Debian) |

**Why it is a bug, not a style issue:**
AGENTS.md §"Docker best practices" says: *"Install the security updates of the base image before
the tools. The official image can be days behind the security repository of the distribution."*
The CVE table in AGENTS.md lists active vulnerabilities (e.g. CVE-2026-111943 trust-store flaw)
that are fixed by `apt-get upgrade -y`. Without it, each rebuilt image inherits whatever packages
are in the `latest` pull of the base image at that moment.

The pattern is also internally inconsistent. `rust-ci/Dockerfile` comments this requirement
explicitly ("Install the security updates of the base image before the tools. The official image
can be days behind the security repository of the distribution.") and runs `apt-get upgrade -y`,
but `rust-desktop/Dockerfile` — a sibling image with the same base — does not.
Likewise, `android/Dockerfile` and `java-ui-browser/Dockerfile` both start from `eclipse-temurin`
on Ubuntu, but only `android` has the upgrade step.

**Evidence:**

`rust-ci/Dockerfile` line 9:
```
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get upgrade -y \
    && apt-get install ...
```

`rust-desktop/Dockerfile` line 4 (missing):
```
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential ca-certificates ...
```

`android/Dockerfile` line 35 (has upgrade):
```
RUN test "$(dpkg --print-architecture)" = amd64 \
 && apt-get update \
 && apt-get upgrade -y \
 && apt-get install ...
```

`java-ui-browser/Dockerfile` line 16 (missing):
```
RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
       ca-certificates curl gnupg unzip \
```

**Recommended fix:** Add `apt-get upgrade -y` after `apt-get update` in the first `RUN` step of
each affected Dockerfile, before any `apt-get install`. Use `--build --pull --no-cache` on the
next build. Follow the existing comment pattern from `rust-ci` and `android`.

### H-2 · `ci/test-built-image.sh` java-eks smoke test does not verify HTTP 200

**File:** `ci/test-built-image.sh`
**Lines:** java-eks `case` branch (approximately lines 73–96)

**Bug description:**
The GitLab CI smoke test uses `wget -q -O /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:8080$path"` to check each
endpoint. `wget` exits 0 for any 2xx response AND for redirects (3xx), because it follows them by
default. It never checks whether the final status is 200.

The equivalent check in `test-images.sh` (the GitHub Actions path) correctly uses curl to capture
and assert the exact HTTP status:
```bash
# test-images.sh (correct)
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "http://127.0.0.1:${port}${path}")
echo "$path $code"
[[ "$code" == "200" ]]
```

```sh
# ci/test-built-image.sh (incorrect)
wget -q -O /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:8080$path"
echo "$path 200"     # always printed, status is not actually 200-verified
```

**Why it is a bug, not a style issue:**
AGENTS.md §"Layout of an image directory" says: *"Keep that script and `test-images.sh` in
agreement."* The two scripts are supposed to test the same thing. The GitLab CI path can pass on
a 302 redirect while the GitHub Actions path correctly fails. The `echo "$path 200"` hardcodes
the string `200` regardless of the actual server response, so the output misleads anyone reading
the CI log into thinking the status was verified.

AGENTS.md smoke-test table says `java-eks` must return HTTP 200 from `/api/health`, `/api-docs`,
and `/swagger-ui/index.html`.

**Recommended fix:** Replace each `wget -q -O /dev/null` check in the `java-eks` branch of
`test-built-image.sh` with a curl call that captures and asserts the HTTP status code, matching
the logic in `test-images.sh`. If `wget` must be used (some minimal containers lack curl),
add `--server-response` and grep the `HTTP/` header for `200`.

## Medium

### M-1 · `rust-desktop/Dockerfile` — pipe without `SHELL pipefail`, hadolint DL4006

**File:** `rust-desktop/Dockerfile`
**Line:** `echo "$binstall_sha  /tmp/binstall.tgz" | sha256sum -c -`

**Bug description:**
`rust-desktop/Dockerfile` has no `SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]` instruction
anywhere in the file. The cargo-binstall installation step uses a pipe:
```dockerfile
RUN set -eu; \
    ...
    echo "$binstall_sha  /tmp/binstall.tgz" | sha256sum -c -; \
```

Without `pipefail`, if the left side of the pipe exits non-zero, the right side (`sha256sum`)
receives empty or truncated input and may fail cleanly with an error about a missing checksum,
but the build does not abort on the left-side failure alone.

AGENTS.md §"Docker best practices" says: *"If a `RUN` instruction has a pipe, put
`SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]` before it. … hadolint reports a pipe without this
`SHELL` instruction as DL4006."*

The sibling file `rust-ci/Dockerfile` correctly has `SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]`
before its equivalent pipe.

**Why it is a bug, not a style issue:**
The `.hadolint.yaml` does NOT ignore DL4006, so running `hadolint` on this file (as AGENTS.md
requires before each commit) would report this as an error. AGENTS.md says: *"Fix the findings
in the lines that you change."*

**Recommended fix:** Add `SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-o", "pipefail", "-c"]` before the `RUN` step
that contains the pipe, matching the pattern in `rust-ci/Dockerfile`.

### M-2 · `compilers/Dockerfile` — missing architecture check and no checksum for DMD binary

**File:** `compilers/Dockerfile`
**Lines:** The DMD download block (~lines 15–18 of the combined RUN)

**Bug description (two closely related issues):**

**(a) No architecture guard:**
The DMD `.deb` URL contains `_amd64` hardcoded:
```dockerfile
curl -fsSLo /tmp/dmd.deb \
  "https://downloads.dlang.org/releases/2.x/$DMD_VERSION/dmd_$DMD_VERSION-0_amd64.deb"
```
There is no `test "$(dpkg --print-architecture)" = amd64` guard before this download.
AGENTS.md §"Docker best practices" says: *"If a download is for one architecture, check
`dpkg --print-architecture` or `uname -m` in the build. Stop the build on an architecture
without a checked download."*
Every other Dockerfile in the repository that downloads an amd64-only binary adds this guard
(e.g. `android/Dockerfile` line 34, `document-tools/Dockerfile`, `web-qa/Dockerfile`).

**(b) No checksum verification:**
The downloaded `.deb` is installed directly with `apt-get install`. The dlang.org release page
publishes SHA-256 checksums for each `.deb` file, but the Dockerfile does not verify them.
AGENTS.md §"Version policy" says: *"Downloaded tool archives: use a stable release. If a
checksum is available, verify it."*

**Why they are bugs, not style issues:**
(a) Without the guard, a build on a non-amd64 host would attempt to install an incompatible
package, causing a silent corruption or a confusing install error rather than a clear
"unsupported architecture" message.
(b) Without a checksum, a compromised or corrupted DMD package is installed without detection,
violating the supply-chain integrity rule stated in AGENTS.md.

**Recommended fix:**
Add `test "$(dpkg --print-architecture)" = amd64` before the download. Pin the `DMD_VERSION`
to an `ARG` with a known-good value, fetch the corresponding checksum from dlang.org, and
verify it with `echo "$sha256  /tmp/dmd.deb" | sha256sum --check` in the same `RUN` instruction.

### M-3 · `rust-ci/Dockerfile` and `rust-desktop/Dockerfile` — `--disable-telemetry` missing on most `cargo binstall` calls

**Files:** `rust-ci/Dockerfile` and `rust-desktop/Dockerfile`

**Bug description:**
AGENTS.md §"Docker best practices" says: *"Disable the telemetry, the analytics, and the update
checks of each tool. … A test run must not send usage data to a vendor."* It names
`cargo binstall --disable-telemetry` as an example.

In `rust-ci/Dockerfile`, the flag is present only on the `sqlx-cli` invocation:
```dockerfile
# has --disable-telemetry:
cargo binstall --no-confirm --only-signed --disable-telemetry \
    --strategies quick-install sqlx-cli

# missing --disable-telemetry:
cargo binstall --no-confirm --strategies crate-meta-data,compile \
    sccache cargo-nextest cargo-audit
cargo binstall --no-confirm --strategies crate-meta-data \
    cargo-tarpaulin cargo-llvm-cov cargo-deny cargo-mutants
```

In `rust-desktop/Dockerfile`, the only binstall call has no `--disable-telemetry`:
```dockerfile
cargo binstall --no-confirm --strategies crate-meta-data,compile sccache cargo-tarpaulin
```

**Why it is a bug, not a style issue:**
The `cargo-binstall` tool sends anonymous usage statistics by default. AGENTS.md explicitly
requires all tools to disable this behavior when running in a build or CI context. Omitting the
flag on two out of three calls in `rust-ci` (and the only call in `rust-desktop`) means CI
builds send telemetry to the cargo-binstall upstream on every image build.

**Recommended fix:** Add `--disable-telemetry` to all `cargo binstall` invocations in both files.

### M-4 · `docker-images.yml` — `trivy-action` pinned to a mutable version tag, not a commit SHA

**File:** `.github/workflows/docker-images.yml`
**Line:** `uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0.36.0`

**Bug description:**
The workflow has an inline comment immediately before the action reference:
```yaml
        # Pin this action to a full commit SHA for better supply-chain security.
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0.36.0
```

The comment states the requirement but the code contradicts it — `@v0.36.0` is a Git tag, which
is mutable. A repository owner can move it to point at a different (potentially malicious)
commit without changing the workflow file.

All other third-party action references in the same workflow also use version tags
(`actions/checkout@v7`, `docker/login-action@v4`, `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v4`),
so this is a systemic gap, but the inline comment specifically calls out `trivy-action` as
requiring a SHA pin.

**Why it is a bug, not a style issue:**
The code and the comment directly contradict each other. The comment was added specifically to
document a security requirement. The intent is clear and the implementation is wrong.
AGENTS.md §"GitHub Actions" says: *"Pin this action to a full commit SHA for better
supply-chain security."*

**Recommended fix:** Replace `@v0.36.0` with the full commit SHA of the `v0.36.0` tag:
```
git ls-remote https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy-action refs/tags/v0.36.0
```
Use the resolved SHA as the pin, e.g. `uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@<sha>  # v0.36.0`.
Apply the same fix to the other third-party actions for consistency.

## Appendix: additional observations (not bugs, noted for completeness)

- **`crossplane/Dockerfile` final stage** uses `amazon/aws-cli:latest` (Amazon Linux, `dnf`).
  The `dnf install -y tar gzip` step runs without `dnf upgrade` first. The AGENTS.md upgrade rule
  is written in terms of `apt-get`, and Amazon Linux images have their own release cadence, so
  this is a judgment call rather than a clear-cut rule violation. Worth reviewing.

- **`postgres-vector-graph/Dockerfile` extensions build stage** uses `postgres:18` (Debian) and
  runs `apt-get install` without `apt-get upgrade -y`. As a build stage whose artifacts are
  copied to the final image, the security impact is lower, but the pattern is still inconsistent.

- **`allure/Dockerfile` download stage** (first `FROM debian:stable-slim`) installs `curl` without
  `apt-get upgrade -y`. Build-stage curl is used only to fetch release archives; the stage's
  packages are not in the published image.

- **`run-rootfs.sh`** supports at most two user-facing `--bind` arguments (via `bind1`/`bind2`
  variables). All current callers use at most one, so this is not a current breakage, but it is a
  undocumented capacity limit that could cause a cryptic error if a new smoke test needs two binds.
